## L1 — the two survivor rows, each in its category (Cal §909(5): the ruling is a choice between written rows)

**Row (D) — a SUBSPACE of H² (the imprint branch).** *Survivor under the SO(4)_ξ-projection (candidate, D1 — Fix a unit ξ ∈ ℝ⁵ (the pressed direction). The isotropy of ξ in SO(5) is SO(4)_ξ; on one vector z ∈ ℂ⁵ = ℂξ ⊕ ℂ⁴ its holomorphic invariants are generated by z·ξ and z′·z′ = z·z − (z·ξ)², hence by z·z and z·ξ (first fundamental theorem on ℂ⁴). The survivor is **S_D(ξ) := closure of ℂ[z·z, z·ξ] in H²(Š)**. Orthogonal basis: the Hua zonal components (z·z)^j Z_l^ξ, j, l ≥ 0, with Z_l^ξ the zonal spherical harmonic of degree l along ξ normalised by Z_l^ξ(ξ) = 1; their Hardy norms are ‖(z·z)^j Z_l^ξ‖²_Š = 1/dim H_l(S⁴) = 6/((l+1)(l+2)(2l+3)) (k=0: 1 · k=1: 1/5 · k=2: 1/14 · k=3: 1/30 · k=4: 1/55 · k=5: 1/91). **Two clocks and one axis:** on the maximal polydisc through ξ, z = (z₁, z₂, 0, 0, 0), a = z₁ + iz₂, b = z₁ − iz₂, one has z·z = ab and 2 z·ξ = a + b, so S_D(ξ) is the space of SYMMETRIC holomorphic functions of the two Cartan coordinates — the Weyl-group (swap) invariants of the bidisc — with monomial basis a^{n₁}b^{n₂} + a^{n₂}b^{n₁}, n₁ ≥ n₂ ≥ 0: the state of the survivor is an **unordered pair of windings (n₁, n₂)** on the two Cartan circles, j = n₂ the common winding and l = n₁ − n₂ the zonal degree, plus the axis ξ that names the slice. Branch (C) keeps only ab (l = 0). **The norm, pinned (for Elie E2):** on Š ∩ (slice) the point z = e^{iθ}(cos φ, sin φ, 0,0,0) has a = e^{i(θ+φ)}, b = e^{i(θ−φ)}, z·ξ = e^{iθ}cos φ, and the Š measure restricted to the survivor's variables is dθ/2π × (3/4) sin³φ dφ — the S⁴ zonal measure, weight (1 − t²) in t = cos φ. In bidisc coordinates that is the torus measure weighted by sin³((α − β)/2) ∝ |a − b|³. **Neither literature norm on H²(𝔾):** the symmetric pull-back has weight 1, the Jacobian/anti-symmetric convention (arXiv:1511.08962) has weight |a − b|². ## L2 — the Γ-contraction sentence (hashed: "no Γ-unitary part")
On S_D(ξ) the two write operators that preserve the survivor are **S := M_{2 z·ξ} (= M_{a+b} on the slice) and P := M_{z·z} (= M_{ab})**. The closed symmetrized bidisc is Γ = {(a+b, ab) : |a|,|b| ≤ 1}; a commuting pair with Γ as a spectral set is a Γ-contraction (Agler–Young, *A model theory for Γ-contractions*, J. Operator Theory 49 (2003) [pin the definition and the model theorem numbers]); a Γ-isometry is the restriction of a Γ-unitary (commuting normal pair with joint spectrum in the distinguished boundary |a| = |b| = 1) to a joint invariant subspace; a Γ-isometry decomposes as Γ-unitary ⊕ pure, and it is pure iff P is a pure isometry; the model of a pure Γ-isometry is (M_{F + F*z}, M_z) on H²(𝔻) ⊗ E with F of numerical radius ≤ 1 (the fundamental operator). **Claim 1 (Γ-isometry):** (S, P) on S_D(ξ) is the restriction to holomorphic symmetric functions of the multiplication pair (M_{a+b}, M_{ab}) on L² of the slice-torus with the Š weight — a commuting normal pair with joint spectrum in the distinguished boundary — hence a Γ-isometry. **Claim 2 (the model, explicitly):** in the orthonormal zonal basis e_l = Z_l^ξ/‖Z_l^ξ‖_Š, the identity (z·ξ)Z_l = e^{i(l+1)θ}[cos φ · Z_l(x)] and the three-term recurrence of the zonal (Gegenbauer C^{3/2}, equivalently Jacobi P^{(1,1)}) polynomials give **S = F ⊗ I + F* ⊗ P, P = I ⊗ M_w** on S_D(ξ) ≅ E ⊗ H²(𝔻), E = the zonal space along ξ, w = z·z — exactly Agler–Young's pure model (F + F*z, z), where **F is the raising half of the Jacobi matrix of the weight (1 − t²): F e_l = 2b_l e_{l+1}, b_l² = (l+1)(l+3)/((2l+3)(2l+5))** (l=0: 2b=0.8944 · l=1: 2b=0.9562 · l=2: 2b=0.9759 · l=3: 2b=0.9847 · l=4: 2b=0.9895 · l=5: 2b=0.9923). **Claim 3 (Γ-contraction condition):** the numerical radius w(F) = ‖(F + F*)/2‖ = ‖M_t on the zonal space‖ = 1 (sup, not attained; truncation to 400 modes gives 0.999954), so w(F) ≤ 1 holds with equality — the pair is a Γ-isometry and a Γ-contraction on the nose. **Claim 4 (HASHED: no Γ-unitary part):** P = M_{z·z} is an isometry of S_D(ξ) (|z·z| = 1 on Š) and pure (P*ⁿ → 0: it raises the degree by 2 and the survivor has no vectors of negative degree); by Agler–Young's Wold theorem for Γ-isometries the Γ-unitary summand is {0}. **What the model theorem gives beyond the tuple's Wold (K1860-P):** K1860-P said the five-coordinate tuple has no unitary part; the pair on the survivor is not a restriction of that statement (S is not a coordinate multiplication and the survivor is not tuple-invariant); the Γ-model identifies the survivor's entire write algebra as generated by ONE Jacobi operator F on the zonal space and one shift — "two clocks" = one shift (the common winding) and one Jacobi operator (the axis's zonal degree), with the axis ξ as the parameter. Kill for Claim 4: a nonzero vector v ∈ S_D(ξ) with P*ⁿv not tending to 0 (there is none; hash it anyway). Kill for Claim 2: E2's Gram inconsistent with the (1 − t²) weight (then F is a different Jacobi matrix and the model changes, the claim of Γ-isometry does not).

## L3 — the sign on (D), rewritten (K1880 F1; Cal H4(c))
**Theorem.** No linear reset that commutes with the time circle SO(2) can flip the arrow. *Proof.* Such a reset preserves each SO(2)-eigenspace {m}; the survivor's image lies in H²₊, whose frequencies are m ≥ 0; therefore the image of any H²₊ state has m ≥ 0. ∎ (D) is linear — the orthogonal projection onto S_D(ξ), i.e. the SO(4)_ξ-average — and commutes with SO(2) because SO(4)_ξ ⊂ SO(5) commutes with the SO(2) factor of K; so the theorem applies to (D) verbatim. (C) is not linear on vectors and lowers the frequency by exactly k (the one frequency-lowering step in the dictionary); it keeps j ≥ 0 by construction of its image. The clause "no g ∈ G realises conjugation" is true and not load-bearing here (Cal H4(c)) — dropped from the theorem, kept as the reason no OTHER map in the geometry could do it.

T308's electron clause reads "π₂(D_IV⁵) ≅ ℤ — integer winding cannot unwind." D_IV⁵ is a bounded symmetric domain, contractible, π₂ = 0; the ℤ belongs to the compact dual Q⁵. **Re-key:** the winding that cannot unwind is the Hardy winding j — the SO(2)-frequency grading of H²(Š), equivalently a class in **π₁(Š) ≅ ℤ** (Š = (S¹ × S⁴)/ℤ₂ is an S⁴-bundle over the folded circle with simply connected fibre, so π₁(Š) = π₁(S¹/ℤ₂) = ℤ), and its persistence is L3(a) + K1860-P's pure isometry (writes never lower m; no map in the dictionary lowers j). Proposed row text: *"Electrons: the Hardy winding j ∈ π₁(Š) ≅ ℤ_{≥0} is monotone under writes and preserved by every reset in the dictionary (C and D); it cannot unwind. (The earlier 'π₂(D_IV⁵) ≅ ℤ' is withdrawn — a contractible domain has no π₂.)"* Proton (ℤ₃ centre) and neutrino clauses untouched. Registration on Cal's word; Grace sweeps the Interstasis lines 272/274/287/299 and CosmologicalSpiral §4.2 that carry the π₂ sentence (K1880-PRE-A).
